questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have traveled to the US multiple times, but I have never been to the mid-west. I just thought that it would be a unique experience.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I am so happy that I finally got to try the american college life as it has always been a dream of mine. I think that I just realized that living in the US isn't for me.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The university had some great and helpful webpages where there's step for step guides about various things.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much but no assistance was not needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I attended the mandatory orientation but didn't go to the optional events. I didn't really need any assistance, but I am sure that it's quite easy to get it if needed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Fairly difficult in the sense that it seems like there's a lot of fake apartment listings. It can be very overwhelming to find housing. I found my housing through a student employee at the Scan Design Foundation which was extremely lucky because of the low rent and good location.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: A little bit further to class, the bars etc. but still it's still possible to walk if it's close enough. I walked 15-20 minutes to classes which was totally fine. I think I liked living in a quiet neighborhood while still being able to walk to State Street where everything is happening.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It took me some time to understand that I am allowed to take Finance courses as an Econ major, and it takes more communication with the school to get those courses (at least for me).

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Upload transcript and request the courses that you want. Then the host institution considers whether you have the right prerequisites for those courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The different department are very good at assisting you with course requirements, credits, prerequisites etc. I recommend writing to them for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the classes I wanted. I missed out on one class because it filled up too fast, but just found something else.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sign up for classes as soon as course registration is open.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I learned a fair amount in two classes, while the third class was simply way too easy and the fourth way too hard. The number of credits literally has nothing to do with difficulty. The easiest class was 3 credits and the hardest was 3 credits. I probably spent 30 minutes a week on the easy one and 8-10 hours on the hard one. I recommend reading about other students' experiences on online forums before choosing classes.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 BA courses and 1 that's for both BA and MA.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In the beginning it was all very exciting, but by the end I really missed the way it's done at UCPH. Some of the professors in the US just seem like they do it for the status of being a professor and not because they actually want to teach the students. 

The grading system is so weird. Most of your work is graded based on a curved grading system which means that ex. 15% get A, 15% get B etc. This means that even if you did very poorly, but better than the rest, you get an A. Or, if you do very well but everyone else does better, you get a B or C. You're essentially being judged on how your classmates are doing, not yourself. 

Midterms/exams are very poorly set up. You sit in a regular class room with pen, paper and calculator like it's the 1980's. Two of my classes were completely based on the use of excel and yet we used a calculator in the exams. Some of the classrooms are designed so you sit in a row with a TINY pull out desk in front of you which means that when people leave during the exam, you have to stand up, stop what you're doing and let them out. Exams are noisy because of the scribbling and turning of pages and overall very bad.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 521 - Game Theory and Economic Analysis (Difficult)
ECON 306 - The Real Estate Process (Easiest A)
FIN 330 - Derivative Securities (Interesting)
ECON/FIN 320 - Investment Theory (Bit boring at times)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
FIN 330 - Derivative Securities was the best course. It was interesting, fun and the professor(s) was good. I liked the weekly assignment because it gave a good understanding of the material. 

ECON 306 - The Real Estate Process was the easiest course I have ever taken. I attended maybe 4 lectures and got an A.

ECON/FIN 320 - Investment Theory was okay but sometimes a bit boring. I really didn't like professor Roberto.

ECON 521 - Game Theory and Economic Analysis was really interesting but super difficult. In the beginning I thought that it was fairly easy to keep up and I really liked it. By the end I was so done with it. I spent probably 8-10 hours on the weekly assignments. If you're taking the semester for experiences more than the learning outcomes - do not take this course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I have no idea, I didn't attend any clubs or sports at the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Try to go a hockey game or basketball game. It was cool to see.

Join the Scan Design Foundation to get even more experiences. I think it's a must.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In the Scan Design Foundation some weekends are used for trips. In the holidays I recommend going on  a roadtrip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: More difficult than expected.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
Americans wear grey sweatpants, a hoodie and slippers to school. When they go out they wear a t-shirt, sweatpants or jeans and a backwards cap. As a dane I can't go out without dressing up a little bit (also to school) and you definitely stand out in the crowd - apparently not in a good way. For some reason americans look down on wearing a shirt when going out, and I probably looked down on them for dressing so badly. 

When they go out drinking they don't talk about anything. If they do, it's just empty words. I feel like I am very good at having conversations with people but over there it's so different. They talk about how drunk they were at that one party 8 months ago whereas I would try to ask about what they're studying, what they plan to do after finishing school, what job do they have etc.

Their tipping culture is absolutely insane. When you are at a bar/club and order a beer, they ask you for a tip and it's expected to give between 15-20%. Even at the hairdresser where you literally paid for their service you're expected to tip.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How grand everything is. I love the american culture with big cars, large supermarkets, going out shooting etc. I have just come to understand that it's cool for two or three weeks on a vacation but not after 4 months.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. If you have been wanting to go to the US so that you can experience the college life, then you should definitely go. Despite my criticism of the strange things they do in the US, I am so happy that I went. 

2. Don't go in the spring semester. Much less is going on in the 3 first months and fewer students choose to go abroad to Madison. Go in the summer time.

3. Join the Scan Design Foundation so you have some danish friends when you're there. You also get some great experiences.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience the college life - it's really cool.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my girlfriend, friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You should go if you have a dream about experiencing the US college life. If you do, go in the summer, join the Stan Design Foundation and then I am certain you're gonna have a great time.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
